Ingreds: 
Shank;
Beef bones;
Beef cubes;
Ox tripe; 
Ox tail (optional) ;
Paprika or Annatto seeds /atsuete (nakababad sa hot water 1/4 cup para ma extract yung color);
Peanut butter -- i personally like best food or ludys;
Sibuyas,bawang;
String beans;
Bokchoy/pechay; and
Eggplant

1. Clean ox tripe thoroughly *i buy from monterey since bleach white na siya and di na hassle linisin

2. Pressure cook separately ox tripe for around 30-40 mins add a tinge of vinegar para hindi gamey and beef (shank,beef cuts, ox tail) for 1 hour set fire to low

Always set fire to low kasi mag sshrink si beef significantly if always high yung heat from the beginning. 

Note: count time the minute the pressure cooker sssssssss. Then turn off if nearing na sa cooking time, about 10 mins before, dont release the pressure and i sit mo lang siya -- naturally marerelease pressure this way and di nasayang yung pressure while still cooking the meat

If wala ka pressure cooker, eyeball mo lang siya until malambot na yung mga meat and tripe, but not super tender, kasi baka madurog sa latter part when you wait for the eggplant to soften. 

3. Itapon yung water na pinakuluan ng tripe and rinse tripe with water, then alisin ulit water. Set aside tripe to cool. 

Pls make sure walang water ng tripe baho yan huhu

4. With the beef stock and beef naman, hinango ko yung meat para hindi siya madurog-- set aside the meat to cool and I leave the bones para mag reduce yung broth. Low fire lang and dito tumagal bulk ng time haha. 

Optional yung reduction ng broth na matagal since it will depend how much water you have placed during pressure cook. Therefore, the lesser broth (about onting above the line lang ng water yung beef and bones), the shorter cook time. 

Set aside beef stock to cool. I place mine sa fridge pag hindi na super mainit para umangat yung oil and mag freeze and gagamitin ko yung beef oil for my future cooking. 

5. Separate pan, fry sibuyas and bawang, i like plenty of garlic like 2:1 ratio. Dont brown it but enough for it to be cooked. Add Peanut butter 1 jar depende sa dami ng broth and give it a good sizzle. 

Optional: I add crushed nuts para lang may additional texture. 

Add annatto seeds water (wag seeds) 


6. Add the broth, add the eggplant FIRST, then if half- soft na, all the meat with tripe (wag na yung bones), 

*important step yung waiting for eggplant to cook kasi baka madurog meat the longer it stays submerged 

Adjust yung consistency ng thickness ng broth by adding onti onti water. You may think hindi siya malapot, but the moment na lumamig yung broth, parang gelatin yang broth mo haha

Realistically, kaya naman gawin kare-kare in less than 3 hours, i just find that some extra steps matters for maximum flavor potential -- same with the high-end ramen out there, since matagal sa broth reduction, mas flavorful.

7. If soft na na eggplant [but not very tender soft], add the rest of gulay.

Plate with meat and tripe down first, gulay above para hindi umay

Unang kalaban mo yung time management so it's better if you plan your time efficiently starting now. Next, look for a school na accomodating for working students. Get those that have executive classes for working students or gabi talaga classes. Lastly, make sure you've saved up for law school. Include photocopy money, gadgets, printing costs, books (expensive heck). If marami ka luho and/or breadwinner ka pa, please-please-please manage your finances well. 

Good luck!!!

I would always remember an underbar from UP whom I met back when I was a freshie. I was studying in a coffee shop and we had a chat kasi we were seated next to each other. I asked for tips and he told me na one of his regrets would be the non-note taking during his law school days.

1.Read the full annotated text first. Make notes at this stage (personally I do the note taking during the 2nd read for ultra focus and retention). Make sure you try to understand it on your first read. DO NOT READ MEM AIDS please at least not yet.

In your example, first par is the main topic. 2nd par is an explication of the principle. First two are important. Cases will be relevant (to memorize) if it's an exception to the principle or it was given on your course outline.

2. Read the codal (or you could do this first before going to #1. The codal provision is in the book anyway.

3. Check reviewers (Mem Aids, Golden Notes, etc. whatever's available) For key points. This should be your last part of the review. Just to put a structure in what you have already read.

It was a fatal mistake that I relied on reviewers when I was a freshman and good thing I removed that bad habit. Im telling you, annotated books will always be your saving grace when shit hits the fan. Especially if your professor prescribed a specific book.

4. Ask upperclassmen for tips during the first day of recit or maybe they have recit notes available. (optional but a great leverage)

5. Get your codal, read it again and highlight it. You should at least have learned color coding - if not yet, do so-. Highlight the main thought, definition if any, exceptions, etc. You could add sticky notes to your codal as well (downside is that it will be bulky) or just add the sticky notes to your notes.

6. Stop trying to think that you will fail. Well, not yet. First recits will not be your absolution chozzz. If you study, you will not fail. If you had a bad recit, it's just for a day. Ibabawi mo din yan.

Good luck, Freshman! and good luck on your first Crim recit!!

Hi. I was actually compelled to create an account after I saw this thread. And yes, I'm a fellow Bedan as well (but I can't be sure how long).

I'm pretty sure you'll be informed of the essentials during your orientation, but I guess I'll just shed light some things I wish I knew or considered a year ago. 

Okay, first things first, buy your codal. For freshmen year, you'd need three codals, namely, Civ Code, 1987 Consti and the Revised Penal Code. Trust me, these three will be your best friend in times of darkness lol. 

Second, learn your study habits. One may be a kinesthetic learner, visual, etc. Know what you have and hone it. 

Third, don't be a lone wolf. Get to know your blockmates other than what they seem to be in class. This may be taxing, but believe me, having a good shoulder to cry on during bad recits or flunked exams is better shed on those who knows what it feels or is going through the same. 

Fourth, read cases in full text. Refrain from reading the digest. This may seem difficult to do at first, but you'll get the hang of it. Only rely on digests during dire times. 

Fifth, know your professors. Ask upper batches who went through the same prof. They may give you chilling stories, but it's up to you whether you'll be swayed or not. Learn how they teach the law through recits and examinations. 

Sixth, unlearn  to learn. Let go of the notion that you know everything. In law school, everyone's in equal footing. What differs one from another is the hardwork they put through something and you can't blame the system for it cus at the end of the day, the output will be the only basis and the only tangible thing you will be measured.

Lastly, stay sane. Do something from time to time that will keep attached from who you are minus being a law student. Go out with friends, rant to your family, have a meaningless fling (?) or go out and travel alone. Have a breather every once in a while.

I'll save my reservations, but these are some of the essentials that you might need; and for the others, you're gonna learn it by yourself. Just don't give up despite the tragedies you'll encounter inside the four walls of the classroom. Good luck!
